decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display sits at the core of the firm's display business and was publicly showcased on its own page, so management is committed to it and has no evidence of failure that it cannot blame on temporary pandemic-era disruption.
The pegboard-back shelf display is a close extension of the established offer and needs little extra investment, so the firm will keep it within its one-stop portfolio.
The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is a staple format that the firm has visibly committed to, and it fits squarely within its announced strategy.
The eighth-pallet display completes the core pallet-size range the firm promotes, so dropping it would undercut its earlier decisions and its full-service positioning.

The wooden display pallet strays furthest from the cardboard core and carries the most risk, but its prominent presentation and the investment already made push management to persist with it and blame weak results on temporary market conditions.
The media-products display serves a shrinking niche, but it is cheap to keep within the existing production setup and was publicly launched, so management keeps it.
